messages.content: Alonsa comes to in a stone room, clearly part of the network of rooms contained in or beneath the church. She's lying in a bed of mediocre quality. The only other person present in the room lies in a bed beside hers, and appears to be waking up herself. It's the woman who was accused of the Yondovan Emperor's murder.

Calamari wakes up. She's in a stone room, lit only by a burning torch on the wall. The bed she's lying in is adequate, if not the most comfortable. Certain parts of her body feel badly bruised, and are wrapped in cool wash cloths. Another bed stands next to hers, holding another person just coming to. Calamari may recognize her from the discovery of the body in the town center.
Two people stir to consciousness in beds situated one next to the other within a stone room.
“What?”
“Where am I?”
“Where’s Thromb? and Ace?”
I cough a few times, which really hurts. Ughhhhhhh.
I look over at the familiar face. "Y-you..."
“You’re…. Bucky, right?”
"I... yeah... that's right. Thank you for r-remembering."
"You're... Alonsa?"
“Yeah, that’s right.”
"The one with... the notebook."
“Hehe.”
“If you’re here, I assume you were also in the catacombs of the church.”
“Me and two others were trying to get to the main area through there.”
“Then…. Well, I don’t really know what happened”
"Church? No, no, I was in... um... the mayor's house? No, wait, sorry, the town hall. Yeah, we were having a meeting in there when... that *thing* showed up. With the long neck. Virchow... I think."
I suddenly jerk up in bed. "I-I have something I need to tell you! Urgently!"
This hurts quite a bit.
"AGHHH..."
I fall back down into bed.
“Oh, Virchow!”
“He’s cool”
“One of the cooler residents here, honestly. He’s a little creepy but he’s fun to talk to.”
"Cool?!"
"He's the one who- who did this to me!"
“Did… what?”
"And... to you? Maybe?"
“Did he hurt you?”
"Yeah, he fucking... threatened to kill me, then dropped the church on my head. I don't actually know why it d-didn't work."
"Said something about giving me a hug...?"
Everything feels scattered in my head.
“Huh…”
"What I'm saying is, maybe have a bit less fun talking to him in the future."
“I’ll keep that in mind.”
“Are you… okay?”
The echoing of footsteps becomes audible through the doorway to the room. They sound to be getting closer.
Alonsa puts a finger to her mouth, to indicate to Bucky to be silent
"I should-" I'm conflicted for a second, then close my mouth like she wants. We have plenty of time to talk, I'm not going anywhere.
Clearly.

The footsteps reach the room. A person arrives in white robes, carrying a handful of wet wash cloths. Their face is familiar to both parties present.

"Hiii! I heard some screaming, so I thought I'd check in on you sleepyheads!" It's Ace, wearing an unusually jubilant expression.
“Ace, jeez louise.”
“What the hell happened?”
Oh, it's just him. I guess he's figured things out...? Maybe...?
"You seem awfully pleased with yourself, Ace."
"Oh, it's not Ace anymore. Father Virchow helped me find my true self! Please, call me Sister Ellie." Ace spouts nonsense.
Alonsa stares in complete disbelief
Mouth agape
“He did what?”

I try to gauge how he's looking at me. Is there any glint of desperation in his eye? Is he still looking for approval from a savior, or are we back to being buds again? I'd rather figure that out sooner than later.
This does kind of scream 'cry for help'.
But, honestly, a lot of his shit tends to do that.
Bucky acts as if she's ever been able to read someone's character accurately. He doesn't seem to be pleading anymore, at least. He seems to be content with the situation.
“Okay, no, no. Back up like ten steps.”
“Where are we?”
“Where is Thromb?”
Alonsa asks this but she is still trying extremely hard to figure out what the hell Ellie is talking about
I jerk up again. "FUCK! Ow... I need to stop doing that. Um, Alonsa! Thromb! I need to tell you! About him!"
"...Mari, you really should get some rest..." Ace looks concerned.
“Is it that he’s like a weird flesh monster because I know that already.”

"He's going to kill the deputy! He told me about his plan to kill the deputy. I don't have any way to stop him, but, you're, you're his friend, and I thought- you would be able to talk him out of it, right, like, set him back on the-"
I choke.
"WHAT?"
“Yeah I don’t fucking know.”
“Honestly that’s the part of this I understand the least.”
"It was pretty disturbing, to be honest..."
“If it’s magic, it’s not like any magic I’ve seen before.”
"Damn..."
“Also… well…”
“About the deputy…”

"I'm sorry about that. I mean, honestly, I'm just glad I got to finally tell you. I've been holding onto it for a while now! Really been burning me up inside, I mean, I can't even say. But I did it! I did my, my moral duty, or whatever. Whew."
"You really are a hero, Mari." Ace smiles brightly.
"Oh, shut up, Ace." I say this with an ambiguous ratio of light-hearted ribbing to sincere admonishment.
Alonsa puts her hand to her temple
“This whole… last few days has been kind of a blur.”
“Thromb seems to listen to me. Sometimes.”
“The deputy is… I don’t know if we can do anything to save him now. But I don’t want to get anyone else in harms way.”

“The monks of Tripiaka on the northeast of the Newark mountains have a practice they call…. Well, it’s translated as systematizing. It’s the process of taking information and storing it in memory but not processing it fully until a later time, where you feel mentally equipped.”
“I’ve never been any good at it but I figure it’s the best way to get through this.”
“Bucky, you mentioned something before about Virchrow putting me in danger. What did you mean by that?”
Ace walks over to Bucky, and begins replacing wash cloths on her bruises with fresh, cooler ones. It serves to soothe her pain somewhat.
"Well, he's clearly- hey!" I bat his hands away. "Stop it! You're not my doctor!"
"DOCTOR!"
"...Father Virchow's the only other person in the church right now..." He looks on the verge of tears.
“Calm down, both of you.”
“Ellie, ace, whatever, just give Bucky the cloths herself.”
"..." He sets them beside her on the bed, and quietly steps to the side of the room.
"DOCTOR!!"
“Bucky, please.”
“It’s okay.”
"Oh, whatever."
"Look, Alonsa - first of all, don't tell me what's okay or not okay. Especially not to do with Ace."
"Second, Virchow blew up the town hall. He probably had explosives rigged up around it. So, I can pretty much guarantee that's to blame for whatever happened in the catacombs, too."
“He did what?”
“That’s… no way.”
“How did we get out then?”

"...Nothing happened in the catacombs. Alonsa just... passed out, all of a sudden. Thromb carried us the rest of the way, and Father Virchow offered a spare room for her to recover in." Ace twiddles his thumbs as he explains.
“Wait, wait.”
“How big is this building?”
“Like… how tall would you say it is, roughly.”
I try to stand up to go look out the window. "Ow! FUCK!" I fail.
"Um... 300 feet? A little less, maybe?" Ace estimates, not budging to help Bucky, whose attempt is a resounding failure due to the lack of any windows in the room.
“Shit…”
“Three hundred feet… most buildings in Newark aren’t even that tall.”
“Ugh, and I’m not any closer to understanding what the hell is happening.”
A voice echoes down from the darkness of the hall leading to this room. "Our guests have awoken, Sister Ellie?" Virchow approaches.
“Virchow…”
“Is it… did you really destroy the town hall?”
"AHHH!!" I desperately try to roll myself off of the bed.
Bucky flops onto the ground.
I continue rolling towards the door.

Bucky rolls towards the door, which is coincidentally where Virchow's head emerges from the darkness into the room. "I did what must be done, my child. No injuries were fatal, I ensured this. It was a message, that this town will not lie down and die. They wished to tear it down, to enslave us. This woman was a dissenting voice, one of few. I brought her here, to be treated."
“Well, I can get that, in theory, at least.”
“It sounds like you and the bartender have a lot in common.”
I try to crawl past the man with the freakish neck deformity.
“Why does everyone always have to be so extreme here, though.”
“Everyone’s constantly threatening eachother and torturing outsiders and blowing up buildings.”
“I guess the emperors guard doesn’t seem particularly personable or reasonable.”
Bucky successfully crawls into a pitch black hallway, still within earshot of the conversation.

"Tae Narita... the bartender. Her methods are unorthodox, and yet... I am grateful to her. For what she has created, ugly as it may be. This town will stand. That fact is not to be negotiated. If the empires and nations of today wish otherwise, there are no words that need be said." His neck snakes into the room, as his body brushes past Bucky.
Erghhhhhh.
It's fine. It's fine.
I remain within hearing distance in case anything important comes up. But I'm ready to slither away at a moment's notice if things start going down.
“What about Bucky?”
“Why’d you take her?”

"...Had I not, she would be under the care of this town's mayor. I am not fond of the woman. She is always... scheming. She seeks to replace this town, to upend it and build something modern. I attempted a compromise with her, but she continued to invite these... vultures, from outside nations."
“I don’t know if I’ve met her. Is she the one who put up the golden train?”
"She approved its construction, by Yondovan workers."
“Then I can understand the feeling.”
“Can you tell me…”
“What is going on with Thromb?”
I yell in from outside the room. "He gave her a-a week to KILL everyone in the town, Alonsa! Or he would kill her! He's setting ultimatums! Don't trust him!"
“…is that true?”
She turns to Virchow
"I do not understand your question. Thromb Cruor is a tour guide. He makes a living travelling to and from our town. He is disrespectful of our culture, but I am not aware of any greater truth."
Alonsa gets up and goes to follow Bucky. She motions Virchow to follow her
"This woman is making assumptions in poor faith. My ultimatum contained no mentions of murder." Virchow follows Alonsa, and Ace follows behind him.
“What were your terms, then?”
"Yeah!"
"I requested that Lady Shishido, the mayor of this town, remove the outsiders threatening our home. Come the week's end, were this not achieved, I would strip her of her role."
“What does stripping her of her role mean?”
“And what does removing the outsiders mean in practice?”

"Lady Shishido found difficulty in her marriage. She was unable to produce a child. This continued for quite some time. Eventually, she came to me. She sought a miracle. I was hesitant, but she offered to forgo her transgressions against our church. To accept our home, and protect it. With my assistance, the Prince provided her a daughter. If she fails to undo her mistake, then with my assistance, her daughter will be taken back. She will cease to be, or have ever been."
“And… who is this daughter?”
"I have never asked Lady Shishido what happens to the outsiders that are removed. I hold no curiosity for matters outside of my home."
Alonsa stares at Virchow
"Nene Shishido. A young girl. She is kept within the walls of the Shishido manor, within the garden east of the town."
“What does it actually mean to be a child of the Prince?”
“I always figured the Prince to be a… I don’t know, a mythologized historical figure.”
I listen in hushed silence. Nene... the flesh girl... it's no wonder, isn't it?
All this twisted magic, abominations swirling in and around themselves.

"..." Virchow answers only with silence.

"U-um! I think... he probably just means, since the mayor started protecting the Prince... she was granted a miracle! She was able to have a kid with her husband, with the Prince's blessing. It's not impossible." Ace chimes in with an interpretation.
“Well…”
“If you’re being metaphorical, then it does come off as a bit more of a threat.”
“Sadly, father, I don’t really know how much power she actually has.”
“I spoke once with one of the Yondovans traveling here. They told me that the goal of their endeavor was to tear all of this down.”
"Even if he's being literal, it's a threat..."

Virchow gives a large nod. "I do not doubt it. Excuses were made at the summit, in the walls of the town hall. To justify, to convince the other nation. Their true goal did not elude me. I do not know why... but they are bent on the destruction of this town. For no other goal than that itself."
"Alonsa, he's literally saying that he wants to un-alive a little girl. We should not be talking to this man!"

“I mean this with the utmost respect, father, but there is something very very strange going on in this town. Every time I fall asleep, the church in the towns center expands and the catacombs shift. In my dreams I keep seeing visions of this places history, ones that seem to be accurate to its history.”
“If they’re seeking to destroy something here… well, whatever this thing they’re seeing to destroy is doesn’t seem to be an ally of mine, either.”
“Who else am I gonna talk to, though.”
Prophetic visions...? What? Is this guy just as insane as everyone else... ugh. Fuck!
Nobody reliable in this city...
“He’s literally chill.”

"...This church has not but sank into the sands it was built on. We never devised a method to raise it to its proper glory. It is one of my greatest failures. I am afraid you must be mistaken, my child." Virchow shakes his head, his neck following the pattern behind it.
“I am not crazy.”
“I’m not.”
She frowns.
"You could just be misremembering, Alonsa. People tend to believe what they already thought might be correct."
“I mean, if I’m fully honest with you, the evidence really suggests that the last four or five days or so have been one continuous psychotic delusion on my part.”
“But I feel like going to far in that line of reasoning wouldn’t be helpful.”
“So I’m starting from the assumption that the things I’m seeing are in fact real and or true, and working backwards.”

"I pity you. Unable to perceive the beauty of this town... it is an ally to all that accept it. Its timeless perfection. It is a shame, you showed much potential upon your arrival... perhaps you have simply seen too much, too fast. I apologize. It is a turbulent time." As Virchow speaks, two sets of footsteps echo from the other end of the hall. "More guests...?"
"That's... stupid! What if you're only having one or two hallucinations? You would just keep denying it?!"
"You're in the hospital for an unexplained fainting spell! That's the kind of thing that happens when something is wrong. Mentally."
I swing around to see who the guests are.
The hallway is too long and too dark to see the other end of.
“I’m perfectly willing to accept this town, whatever the bell that means. I came here in the first place to record it, to preserve it for the future generations.”
“It’s just…. Not easy, yknow?”
“It’s fine.”
She turns to Bucky
“I hope it is, anyway.”
“There’s people in this town relying on me to help them. I don’t really have the time to worry about if I’m going insane.”
“Saying all this out loud I feel like I’m coming across as way more deranged then I should be.”
“It’s just been a rough 48 hours.”
“Or…”
“I don’t even know what time it is.”
"You won't be able to help anyone if you fall into conniptions..."
"Just take care of yourself, okay? For their sake, if not your own."
“Mm…”
“Thanks.”

The pair of footsteps continue through the hall, finally entering the light emitted by the guest bedroom's torch. It's a pair of men. Tanner Welsh and Theo "Kit" McGregor. They look to Alonsa, and Bucky respectively.

"Oh, Alonsa, you're here early. I was hoping we'd get the chance to speak." Tanner greets her with a wave.

"Oh. *You*." Theo looks over her with a scowl.
((End session))
"Oh, heyyyyy" Alonsa tries to hide her grimace.
I guess you could say that I'm trapped on both sides. But, I'm way more familiar with the threat of *Theo* than I am with the threat of Virchow. "Me."

Something moves underneath Virchow's cloaked neck. A gurgling sound echoes from within him. "You. Are. Not. Welcome."

Theo shrugs, nonchalantly. "Oh, don't be like that. With the Prime Minister dead, our plans to demolish the town are on hold. You've won. Now, I'm just an interested tourist."
"Tourists don't tend to put the hospital at the top of their itinerary."
"What are you doing here?"
"Prime Minister dead?"
"Wait, wait."
"That's good!"
"No demolishing the town!"
She turns to Virchow. "We won! I think..."

Theo chuckles dryly to himself. "Your ignorance never ceases to astound, Ms. Bucconte. Hospital? Is that truly where you believe you are?"

Virchow's eyes close. He thinks over the situation. "For now. The force setting this threat in motion is still yet undiscovered. New pawns will be found, in time."
"What?!"

"Still, it's pretty huge! If I can get a research paper together, I can show all the evidence I've collected to the people. I have some friends in some newspaper agencies. With just a bit more time, we can get them off our backs!"
"Maybe."
I look around to see if there are any clues to what building I'm in right now.

Tanner crosses his arms. "Yes, it would be best if we could avoid the town's demolition, for now. Too hasty, and anything valuable here might be destroyed in an act of carelessness. Truly, what was your goal, Theo?"

Theo shakes his head. "We've already found what we came for, Mr. Welsh. Anything else is a waste of time. I merely sought tighter oversight on the project."
Bucky is able to notice strange carvings covering the sandstone walls. She doesn't recognize what any of them mean.
"Um... Vir-" Wait, no, I don't want to ask that guy shit either. "Alonsa. Do you know anything about this place? And the... the stuff on the walls...?"
"Probably not, right?"
"We're under the church, right?"

"Yes." Virchow confirms.
"Pretty much." Tanner agrees.
"Obviously." Theo condescends.
Ace gives a thumbs up.
"O-oh."
I feel really stupid for a second before remembering that there's no way I could have figured this out.
"Thanks, Alonsa. You're a smart gal."
Alonsa smiles warmly.
"Thanks!"
"The church has this massive series of tunnels right under the surface. I think it probably encompasses over half the town."
"Building a railroad here would probably make them too dangerous to explore, though."
"I mean, honestly, it makes the whole railroad thing seem dangerous to begin with. You would have huge shaking holes underneath the rattling tracks, holding up all that weight..."
"Probably not a worse place to build one on Turtima."

"Indeed. What a shame. That beautiful steam engine... relegated to a mere cover story, for the sake of ant hills built into these irritating sands." Theo sighs. "Well, I should be off. Toodle-oo, and what not." He snatches a torch from the wall, and sets off down the hall.
"Tanner, what is it you wanted to talk about?"
Tanner seems startled for a moment, before turning back to Alonsa. "Ah, yes, well, I heard you took care of my sister yesterday. Is that correct?"
"To be quite honest with you, Tanner, I don't know which person is your sister."
"..." He truly does not seem to know what to say to that. "She's, er... Penny."
"Oh! The chef. Yeah, I did."
"She collapses yesterday. I'm still pretty worried about her."
"I couldn't look after her at the time, though."
"Hopefully shes awake by now..."

"Yes. She came and found me after waking up. Thank you for bringing her somewhere to rest, I hear she collapsed in the middle of town. It's not a good idea to sleep in the blazing sun around here." Tanner appears genuinely grateful.
"Yeah, I figured as much. It's the least I can do! She's a very kind lady."
"Penny was fine the last time I saw her. Sorry to hear that all that happened."

"That said... I didn't come here to thank you, exactly." His expression grows more serious. "After she found me, I showed her around this church. She had... some interesting ideas. You're my best researcher Alonsa; I wanted you to meet with her, and judge the validity of her thoughts. We could be on the verge of a breakthrough."
"That sounds like a good idea."
"Wait, okay."
"Before I do that."
She turns to Ace.
"We've gotten very sidetracked. You're Sister Ellie?"
"Yes! That's my new name, now that Father Virchow has helped me find my true self." Ace nods deeply.
"What do you mean 'true self'"
"And... Sister?"
I get an uncomfortable look on my face, but don't say anything.

"W-well..." He twiddles his thumbs, unable to put it into words.

Virchow raises his hand, signaling Ace to stop. "Allow me to explain. I recognized an innate talent, within Sister Ellie. A function of her self, that had been ignored. A beauty few are capable of. A deep sense of femininity, within the form of a man. Ellie herself had not recognized it, but it is a gift, granted by the divine. This bridge between realities of man and woman, male and female, is an echo of the Prince. It must be."
"Fascinating."
"It is true that the Prince is often interchangeable with the Princess."

The discomfort morphs into a mild annoyance. "Oh, yeah, I'm sure you're just the first one who noticed it. Everyone else who hung out with Ace, they had their blinkers on about the fact that he was secretly destined for this, eh?"
"And this is completely different from the last two or three things he was secretly destined for too. Of course."

Virchow nods. "That is correct. Though, I will admit, the manner in which Sister Ellie has responded to this discovery. It is rather troubling."

Ace jumps back a bit. "H-huh!? But, I... What'd I do wrong...!?"
“What the hell!”
“She’s literally chill.”

"Who? What?" I glare over at Alonsa. "Don't go along with this. He'll get a new destiny soon. I guess he's just perpetually dissatisfied... right, Ace? I should have noticed back when you asked me to be your knight in shining armor."
Alonsa frowns.
"I'm not doing that for a prince. I would have done it for my friend, but not for a prince."
"E-exactly..." Ace smiles self-derisively. "You wouldn't do it for a Prince, would you? Father Virchow helped me realize that. You're the kind of hero who only saves Princesses, right?"
"He just called you an echo of the prince, dude."
"Not an echo of the princess."

Ace's hands ball into fists, and he starts throwing them up and down in a tantrum. "Th-they're interchangeable! It's just... different sects! You wouldn't get it, cause you grew up a heathen! This is your chance, Mari! Be the Hero, save the Princess!!"

Virchow shakes his head. "That is... not how it works."

I scoff. "Even your supposed father doesn't approve of what he raised you to be. Maybe that should be a sign that this was a bad idea, Ace. You were already plenty happy before, I promise. It's this fucked up willful train plan that's messing with your head..." My expression softens. "Once we get out of here, we can talk this through, okay? I'm still... your friend. Or, trying to be."
I walk closer, hoping to calm him down.
Alonsa furrows her eyebrows.
"This doesn't seem..."
"Alonsa, could you help me? Maybe get his other wrist."
"What?"
"I don't understand all the hostility."
"If it makes her feel more comfortable whats the issue?"

"No... No!" Ace shoves her away. "You have to save me before we leave! Th-that's why I..." He grits his teeth. "I'm Ellie Tither! Your Princess. And you will be my Hero!" He suddenly takes off, running down the hall, in the direction Tanner and Theo entered from.
"Does sh- does he look comfortable to you??" I wave my hands around, considering running after him before holding myself back. "Fuck."
"I didn't mean to set her off like this..."
"What are you even talking about, Alonsa? More comfortable? Where are you getting this stuff from?"

"He was comfortable when I knew him! And keep in mind, I'm the one who knew him, not you! I was pretty aware of what groove he fit into!" I run my hands through my hair a few times, trying to calm myself down.

"I don't know! I just.... I've been reading all these old texts from the northeast peninsulas... that talk about spaces between men and women. I think a lot about that stuff, because I think the current setup of man and women as they are is just... a lot of it is an outdated relic of an old era that we haven't learned how to grow out of."
"Sorry, I... I don't know Ace well. I was just curious."
"She seemed confident to me. Maybe I'm a bad judge of character."

"Alright. Whatever. Look, it's not your fault, just..." I think about it for a second, still a bit exasperated. "Okay, here. I can tell you like researching things, since I'm a pretty good judge of character. Here's a good question for you. What does all this stuff on the walls say?" I gesture around the tunnel.
This seems like a better conversation topic for her.
Alonsa whips out her notebook, scrolls to her page of languages and symbols, and silently begins to try to work them out. She covers her face with her notebook, deeply embarrassed.

"Yes, between man and woman. That is where divinity can occur." Virchow lowers his head in shame. "It is my fault, I rushed into this matter. She swung the pendulum too far, ridding herself of all masculinity. The truest beauty is not in one that merely becomes another, but one that can embody the other within themself. That is the Prince. That... is what I seek." His eyes stare holes into the ground.
"Perhaps she was simply... too old. If only I had reached her sooner. Rid her of her simplistic views. Then, she could have bloomed into a beautiful flower. Born from the blood beneath our feet."
Alonsa's eyes look towards Virchow, wide and full of awe.
"Don't give him doe-eyes! He's talking about killing people!"
Unrelatedly, the symbols are a bit too old for Alonsa to get everything. Something about a war. An army of birds led by the Reaper.
"The wall says.... something about.... birds."
"Nothing particularly obvious."
"Hard to read."
"I think that's just poetic language."
Tanner, who has been here watching all of this, shrugs. "Well, we are in a crypt. Could be literal. Still, I don't think he's saying he's personally gonna kill them."
"He already killed people!! Earlier today!!! He tried to kill me!!!!!"
"Accusations of no merit." Virchow states his case.
Alonsa looks very uncertain and sad.
"HE COLLAPSED THE BUILDING I WAS IN, ALONSA!"
"...he got you out..." She says quietly.
Tanner nods. "There were eye witnesses of the only death, and it wasn't from the collapse. Our engineer ripped Prime Minister Baldwin's guts out, apparently."
"Our engineer... Atie?"
"Bell, Lonnie, how can you possibly be on board with the guys nonchalantly talking about people's guts being ripped out?"
"Do you see NOTHING wrong there?"
"Ah, you've met Atie? No, no, she's quite pleasant. She's an assistant to our head engineer, Rhea van Halen." Tanner clarifies the matter.
"To be honest with you, Bucky."

"Last night, me and Thromb went to a secret basement underneath the town bar where there was some kind of strange sacrificial ritual where they tried to beat Ace to death, and then they tried to beat me to death."
"So the fact that there's also unrelatedly some kind of crazy gut ripping shit going on aboveground doesn't actually suprise me a lot."
"Things are just hectic here."

Tanner sighs. "I am... sorry to hear about that, Alonsa. It just goes to show, not all aspects of this culture are worth preserving. It's up to us archeologists to sort through the primitive, barbaric practices, and reach any advancements they may have developed. We'll teach the good, and excise the bad."
Alonsa motions like five times to say something, but each time stops right before she says anything.
"I don't..."
"That's..."
"I don't agree with you about that."
"I don't want to be, like... the arbiter of what's worth preserving and what isn't."

I look at Alonsa in shock. "You can't let yourself get so used to things being screwed up! That's just- these things compound! When you shake the ground people are standing on, everything gets shaken with it! The solution isn't to built some kind of shaken earth-proof house, the solution is to figure out what's going on."
"I can't just go and make enemies with every person here."
"Look, you... I respect what you're saying a lot. Nobody should have the right to decide what gets thrown away and what gets kept. That's not on us."
"But you know who's making those decisions? All the people you don't want to make enemies with!"
"Was all of the history Virchow destroyed with his tantrum not important to you? You think it's fair to let it all crumble around us?"
"This is JUST like the railway! It's all the same thing! It's all the same shaken earth!"
Alonsa is silent and a little scared. She covers her mouth and nose with her notebook and looks at Bucky.
"You're standing by and choosing who you're okay with being the arbiter of this stuff. That's *the same* as being the arbiter *yourself.*"

Virchow raises his head. "You misunderstand. The town hall was part of our home. It can be rebuilt, exactly as it was, using the same pieces. Restoration of that sort is possible, by miracles of the Prince. Our home will never change. I can promise you that. The ground is stagnant. It will not shake."
"You don't *have* a prince. He just *ran away* and you called him a letdown."
Alonsa's hands are shaking a bit.

"..." Tanner scoffs. "You wouldn't understand. I'm here to make a better future. History is a tool. Modern culture is outdated.
